title: GPU econ decision sprint
content:
Sprint purpose and context:
This is a focused 1-week decision sprint to converge on a recommended Dedicated capacity design for Customer Rho's POC. Goals: produce a clear GPU mix recommendation (types + counts), a cost sensitivity envelope, and a small set of autoscaling and fallback rules that SRE/Platform can implement as a follow-up. This doc captures notes from the sprint kickoff, quick empirical sims, heuristics we used, and short action items.

Key constraints from customer brief:
- Target 99p latency for text-generation 128-token responses at tail under 200ms preferred (soft).
- Mixed workload: 60% short chats (~50 tokens), 30% interactive completions (~200 tokens), 10% long-batch analytical jobs (~2k tokens) scheduled off-peak.
- Budget envelope: ~$45k/mo committed to Dedicated for the first 6 months; willingness to supplement with burst/hosted if justified.
- Data residency: private VPC, no external model hosting.

Kickoff takeaways (09/10):
- Customer cares most about predictable p95 latency for user-facing chat; cost per 1k responses is secondary but constrained.
- Accepts occasional graceful degradation (model downscale or degrade to smaller variant) for short windows during large spikes.
- Wants clear observable metrics to tie to cost (tokens/response, GPU-util, queue depth).

Empirical microbenchmarks (developer quick-run, 09/11):
- Models tested: open-m-13b (fp16), open-l-70b (q8), rw-redwood-20b (q4hf).
- Hardware profiled: A100-80GB (m40), H100-80GB (m60), L40s (m20) — numbers below are approximate from our local perf rigs.

Throughput / latency (single stream, cold KV cache):
- open-m-13b @ A100: 1 stream = 60 tps (tokens/sec), 50-token response ~0.83s; batching 4 -> 200ms p95 if prefix cache warm.
- rw-redwood-20b @ H100 q4hf: 1 stream = 45 tps, 50-token response ~1.1s; batching 6 -> p95 210ms if warm.
- open-l-70b @ H100 q8: 1 stream = 25 tps, 50-token response ~2.0s; heavy mem usage, not ideal for many concurrent short chats.

Cost assumptions (public cloud list/hour used for sims):
- A100-80GB reserved equivalent: $3.90/hr (on-demand region-equivalent), commit discount reduces to $2.70/hr (monthly commit plan).
- H100-80GB: $8.50/hr on-demand, commit to $5.50/hr.
- L40s: $2.40/hr on-demand, commit to $1.75/hr.
- Note: actual committed pricing depends on customer contract; these are comparison figures used for internal decisioning only.

Quick cost-per-1M-token proxy (rough):
- open-m-13b on A100 (q4hf batching): 1M tokens ~= $45 (when pooling effectively, steady-state).
- rw-20b on H100 (q4hf): 1M tokens ~= $95.
- open-l-70b on H100 (q8): 1M tokens ~= $220.

Design alternatives considered (high level):
1) Lean reserved A100-only pool + burst to hosted: cheapest, good for 13b-class; risk = underperforming on 20b/70b quality-sensitive requests.
2) Heterogeneous pool (A100 + H100): reserved A100 for baseline, a small H100 reserve for premium traffic + burst; better latency headroom for 20b models.
3) H100-heavy reserved for strict latency SLOs: costly, but single-tier predictable performance for 70b-class.
4) Commit minimal Dedicated + rely on dynamic warm-standby hosted capacity: minimizes capex but increases fragmentation and complexity.

Heuristics and decision matrix used:
- If >25% of responses require 20B+ quality, prefer heterogeneous pool with at least 1 H100 per 8 A100s.
- For p95 latency <300ms on 50-token workloads, require either: a) batching + warmed prefix cache and A100-level kernels OR b) H100 with q4hf for larger models.
- Keep a 20% headroom buffer on GPU effective concurrency to absorb short spikes without triggering scale-up.
- For long-batch jobs (2k tokens), schedule to off-peak (22:00–06:00) into dedicated job queue to avoid interfering with user-facing pools.

Recommended baseline (our converged sprint recommendation):
- Start with heterogeneous pool: 6 x A100-80GB (reserved) + 1 x H100-80GB (reserved, labeled premium).
- Autoscaling policy: allow burst to 2 additional H100s (hosted burst or reserved warm-standby depending on contract) and +3 A100s as burst (pay-as-you-go). Scale triggers:
  - Scale-up A100 by 1 when GPU utilization >75% for 90s AND average queue depth per model >3.
  - Scale-down A100 by 1 when utilization <40% for 5m AND queue depth <1.
  - Promote premium traffic to H100 when request tag premium=true OR model_version in [rw-redwood-20b, open-l-70b] AND p95 latency > target.
  - Fallback policy: if H100 not available, route premium traffic to A100 with reduced max_tokens (e.g., cap at 150 tokens) and optionally a lighter model variant.

SLA and observability windows to implement quickly:
- Dashboards: per-model p50/p95 latency, queue depth, per-GPU concurrency, tokens/sec, cost burn rate per hour.
- Alerting: sustained queue depth >20 for any model for >5m; sustained GPU util >90% for >3m; sudden cost burn spike >2x baseline for 1h.

Cost simulation (example month steady-state):
- Reserved commit cost (6 A100 @ $2.70/hr + 1 H100 @ $5.50/hr) = (6*2.70 + 1*5.50) * 24 * 30 ~= $6,652/mo (note: these illustrative prices assume enterprise commit discounts).
- Burst/overflow (assume 80h H100 and 200h A100 on-demand over month) ~= (80*8.50 + 200*3.90) ~= $3,080.
- Total month = ~$9.7k (steady), well under customer's $45k commit. This indicates space to increase reserved counts or raise model quality.

Why this mix: gives predictable baseline for common short-chat traffic (A100), keeps an H100 for premium/quality-critical paths with predictable latency, and leaves commit headroom to expand without immediate re-contracting.

Open questions / risks:
- Our benchmark data uses a small local rig; cloud variance may shift p95 by +10–30%. We need quick cloud smoke tests in target region (ACTION: Marcus to run 2-day cloud perf sweep using customer's sample prompt set).
- Customer's expectation around 200ms p99 may be unrealistic for 70b-class; align on SLOs and acceptable fallbacks. (ACTION: schedule alignment call with Rho PMs).
- Billing and commitment terms: need finance to confirm allowable price bands and burst allowances. (ACTION: Aisha to loop in Finance, ref CONFLUENCE-ENG-9876).

Immediate next steps (timeline for next 7 days):
- Day 1 (09/17): finalize perf sweep plan and data collection harness (Marcus).
- Day 2–3: run cloud smoke tests across A100/H100 in us-west-2 using 3 prompt mixes (short/interactive/long) (Marcus + Omar).
- Day 4: review results, adjust decision matrix and recommended counts (team sync).
- Day 5: draft customer slide explaining recommended pool, autoscale rules, and cost envelope (Lena to draft).
- Day 7: present to customer and SRE for alignment.

Appendix (notes, heuristics, quick math):
- Effective concurrency estimate: concurrency_per_gpu ~= (GPU_tokens_per_sec * accept_rate_window) / avg_tokens_per_response. We used 40k tokens/sec per A100 at steady pooling in sims; yields x simultaneous short-chat sessions accordingly.
- When sizing, prefer committing to a slightly larger A100 baseline vs H100 because A100s give better cost/throughput for 13b-class and we can route quality-critical to fewer H100s.

Meeting log and quick fragments from sprint chat (unedited):
- "If customer is trying to hit p95 200ms for 50 tokens, we should probably push for warmed prefix cache and small batching — software engineering required, but cheaper than H100 floor." — Lena
- "We should include a plan B that uses hosted API throttle + queueing to protect user-facing latency while background jobs run." — Omar
- "Finance needs to confirm whether we can flex committed GPU hours mid-quarter; this will impact how aggressive we recommend reserve counts." — Aisha

End of doc.
